newsitem.title: USA: Pa. Senate panel to hold hearings on managed care.
newsitem.headline: Pa. Senate panel to hold hearings on managed care.

text.p: Pennsylvania Senate's Public Health and Welfare Committee will hold hearings Friday on a plan to increase consumer protections for managed care programs.
The hearing, slated to be held in Pittsburgh, will review legislation sponsored by Sen. Tim Murphy, R-Allegheny, who serves as vice chairman of the committee.
Murphy said the Pittsburgh hearing is the third of five to be held across Pennsylvania on his "Quality Health Care Protection Act."
Among those scheduled to testify are health care providers, representatives of insurance companies, advocacy groups and health care consumers.
Murphy's proposal, Senate Bill 100, would require managed care plans to provide an easy-to-understand description of coverage to all current and prospective enrollees.

It would also prohibit managed care plans from restricting a provider's ability to discuss treatment options with patients, including options that may be expensive or not covered by the plan. It also prohibits doctors from receiving incentives to withhold treatment.
Murphy said his legislation is prompted by concerns that health maintenance organizations may make financial decisions at the expense of patients' health care needs.

"These protections will strengthen accountability and address key concerns raised by both patients and physicians," Murphy said. "HMOs now have established a place in our health care delivery system. But we have to set down guidelines to ensure that financial concerns don't overshadow the number one concern, which is patient care."
